fullPassage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are (A)[useless / valuable] and unpleasant places, but actually they are (B)[unique / ordinary] ecosystems that must be protected because they provide (C)[numerous / limited] benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 습지가 쓸모없는(useless) 곳이라고 생각할 수 있지만, 실제로는 독특한(unique) 생태계이며, 수많은(numerous) 혜택을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① useless — unique — numerous: 원문 일치. 'but actually'로 역접.
❌ ② valuable(가치 있는): useless의 반의어. 앞에서 부정적으로 본다는 문맥.
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): unique의 반의어. 보호해야 할 '특별한' 생태계.
❌ ④ limited(제한된): numerous의 반의어. 보호 이유가 '많은 혜택'.
det.tip: useless(쓸모없는) ↔ valuable(가치 있는), unique(독특한) ↔ ordinary(평범한), numerous(수많은) ↔ limited(제한된)

questions.passage: The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea. It functions as a natural sponge, (A)[absorbing / repelling] and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an (B)[excellent / mediocre] place to observe more than 400 species of birds. The (C)[exotic / common] pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 카마르그는 물을 흡수(absorbing)하는 천연 스펀지 역할을 한다. 400종 이상의 새를 관찰할 수 있는 훌륭한(excellent) 장소이다. 이국적인(exotic) 분홍 홍학이 가장 유명하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ absorbing — excellent — exotic: 원문 일치.
❌ ① repelling(밀어내는): absorbing의 반의어. 스펀지가 물을 밀어내면 홍수 조절 불가.
❌ ② mediocre(평범한): excellent의 반의어. 400종 이상이면 훌륭한 장소.
❌ ④ common(흔한): exotic의 반의어. '가장 유명한 종'이므로 이국적이 적절.
det.tip: absorbing(흡수하는) ↔ repelling(밀어내는), excellent(훌륭한) ↔ mediocre(평범한), exotic(이국적인) ↔ common(흔한)

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter. For example, the Florida panther has (A)[flourished / declined] in the Everglades. It was nearly (B)[extinct / thriving] in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population had (C)[recovered / diminished] to about 230 by 2017.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 플로리다 퓨마가 에버글레이즈에서 번성했다(flourished). 1995년에 거의 멸종(extinct) 상태였으나, 2017년 약 230마리로 회복했다(recovered).
det.analysis:
✅ ② flourished — extinct — recovered: 원문 일치.
❌ ① thriving(번성하는): extinct의 반의어. '12마리뿐'이므로 모순.
❌ ③ declined(감소한): flourished의 반의어. 번성했다는 맥락에 부적절.
❌ ④ diminished(줄어든): recovered의 반의어. 230마리로 늘어난 것.
det.tip: flourished(번성한) ↔ declined(감소한), extinct(멸종된) ↔ thriving(번성하는), recovered(회복된) ↔ diminished(줄어든)

questions.passage: Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a ①<u>habitat</u> for a number of threatened and endangered species. Furthermore, Upo ③<u>causes</u> floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies ④<u>adequate</u> water to local farmers during droughts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③causes(일으킨다) → prevents(막는다): 우포늪은 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 '막는' 것이지 '일으키는' 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ causes → prevents: 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지한다는 문맥. 'absorbing water'가 단서.
❌ ① habitat(서식지): 멸종 위기 종의 서식지이므로 적절.
❌ ② extinct(멸종된): 딱오기가 거의 멸종 상태이므로 적절.
❌ ④ adequate(충분한): 가뭄 때 농부들에게 충분한 물을 공급하므로 적절.
det.tip: prevents(막다) ↔ causes(일으키다). 습지의 홍수 조절 기능: 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지.

questions.passage: The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become ①<u>powerful</u> and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are ②<u>available</u>. If you have ever seen a ③<u>magnificent</u> image of horses running through water, it is very ④<u>unlikely</u> that they are Camargue horses from this area.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④unlikely(가능성이 낮다) → likely(가능성이 높다): 물속을 달리는 말의 멋진 이미지를 본 적이 있다면 카마르그 말일 '가능성이 높다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ unlikely → likely: 카마르그 말이 물속을 달리는 것으로 유명하므로 가능성이 높다.
❌ ① powerful(힘센): 거친 환경에서 생존하여 힘세졌다는 맥락에 적절.
❌ ② available(이용 가능한): 갈대, 풀, 잡초만 먹을 수 있다는 맥락에 적절.
❌ ③ magnificent(웅장한): 물속을 달리는 말의 이미지를 묘사하므로 적절.
det.tip: likely(가능성이 높은) ↔ unlikely(가능성이 낮은). 'It is very likely that ~' = ~일 가능성이 매우 높다.

questions.passage: The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically ①<u>exposed</u> the people from invaders. Nero sent the military to ②<u>explore</u> the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to ③<u>proceed</u> beyond the Sudd. The Sudd has been ④<u>contaminated</u> by oil spills from oil extraction activities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①exposed(노출시켰다) → protected(보호했다): '장벽(barriers)'이라는 이름에서 알 수 있듯이 침략자로부터 사람들을 '보호'한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① exposed → protected: 'barriers(장벽)' 역할을 했으므로 침략자의 접근을 막아 보호.
❌ ② explore(탐험하다): 네로가 군대를 보내 탐험했으므로 적절.
❌ ③ proceed(나아가다): 병사들이 더 이상 나아갈 수 없었으므로 적절.
❌ ④ contaminated(오염된): 기름 유출로 오염되었으므로 적절.
det.tip: protected(보호하다) ↔ exposed(노출시키다). 'barrier(장벽)'는 외부 침입을 막는 역할.

❌ ② territory(영역): food, water와 병렬로 나오기엔 범주가 다름.
❌ ③ competition(경쟁): 생존에 필요한 것이 아닌 부정적 요소.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 물을 머금는 능력이 홍수 조절(control)에 도움이 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② control(조절): 물을 흡수하고 서서히 방출하므로 '홍수 조절'이 적절.
❌ ① damage(피해): 홍수 피해가 아니라 홍수를 막는 역할.
❌ ③ warning(경고): 경고 시스템이 아니라 자연적 조절 기능.
❌ ④ insurance(보험): 물리적 기능과 무관.
det.tip: flood control(홍수 조절): 습지가 물을 흡수하여 급격한 수위 상승을 막는 기능.

questions.passage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special <u>breed</u>, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and <u>breeding</u> seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 단어의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 카마르그 말은 세계에서 가장 오래된 품종(breed) 중 하나이다. (B) 이동과 번식(breeding) 시즌 동안 에버글레이즈에 의지한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) 품종 — (B) 번식: (A)에서 breed는 명사로 '품종', (B)에서 breeding은 '번식'.
❌ ① (A) 번식 — (B) 품종: 의미가 뒤바뀐 함정.
❌ ② 종류 — 종류: (B)의 breeding seasons는 '번식 시즌'.
❌ ③ 번식 — 번식: (A)의 'a special breed'는 '특별한 품종'.
det.tip: breed: (n.) 품종, 종류 / (v.) 번식하다, 기르다. breeding season = 번식기.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the natural environment in which an animal or plant normally lives"

det.korean: "동물이나 식물이 정상적으로 사는 자연 환경" = habitat(서식지)
det.analysis:
✅ ② habitat(서식지): 동식물이 사는 자연 환경.
❌ ① ecosystem(생태계): 생물과 환경의 상호작용 전체 체계로 더 넓은 개념.
❌ ③ climate(기후): 장기간의 기상 조건.
❌ ④ territory(영역): 동물이 점유하는 지역이지만 자연 환경 전체를 뜻하지 않음.
det.tip: habitat(서식지): 특정 종이 자연적으로 서식하는 환경. habitat ≈ home, dwelling.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the __________ (migrate) and breeding seasons.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이동(migration)과 번식 시즌 동안 에버글레이즈에 의지한다.
det.analysis: migrate(v. 이주하다) → migration(n. 이주/이동). 'during the ___ and breeding seasons'에서 정관사 the와 and breeding(명사)과 병렬이므로 명사형 필요.
det.tip: migrate(v.) → migration(n. 이주) → migratory(adj. 이주하는). 명사 병렬: the migration and breeding seasons.

questions.passage: It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the __________ (important) of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying them.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 습지의 중요성(importance)을 이해했으니 파괴하지 않는 방법을 고려해야 한다.
det.analysis: important(adj. 중요한) → importance(n. 중요성). 'the ___ of wetlands'에서 정관사 the + of 사이에 명사가 필요.
det.tip: important(adj.) → importance(n. 중요성) → importantly(adv.). 'the + 명사 + of' 구조.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the economic value of oil extraction
the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems
the methods to increase urban development
the reasons why climate change is inevitable

det.korean: 생태계 유지에서 습지의 중요성을 이해했으니 파괴하지 않고 사는 방법을 고려해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems: 습지 보존 필요성을 역설하는 결론.
❌ ① the economic value of oil extraction: 석유 추출은 오히려 습지 오염 원인.
❌ ③ the methods to increase urban development: 도시 개발은 습지 파괴 원인.
❌ ④ the reasons why climate change is inevitable: 기후변화 불가피성이 아니라 습지 보존이 주제.
